## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In modern scholarship, the sutta was analyzed extensively by Mark Allon as a case study of mnemonic repetition and prose formulas in the Pali Canon [Allon 1997].

Curated parallels include Chinese translations preserved in the *Dīrghāgama* (DĀ 8), the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 104), and the individual translation T 11 (*Nijutuo fanzhi jing*) [1953]. Within the Pali Canon, parallels and shared thematic pericopes on asceticism are found in the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (DN 8 and MN 12), the *Cūḷadhammasamādāna Sutta* (MN 45), the *Kandaraka Sutta* (MN 51), the *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3.156–162, AN 4.198), with references also occurring in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 15) and *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4). DharmaNexus strongly aligns the text with these Chinese parallels (T 26, T 1, and T 11) and documents thousands of Pali text-reuse matches, most prominently with AN 10, AN 3 (§8.4–8.13), MN 29, DN 9, MN 85, AN 4, AN 6, MN 51, and MN 94 [DharmaNexus].
